notes:
Run 2026-10-21 23:44 UTC to 2026-10-22 01:30 UTC (date field is the task day; most of the measuring ran after midnight UTC) on a 4-vCPU / 15 GB shared VM, so absolute timings are noisy; ratios are the useful signal. grit = main at the commit above (release build, 0.5.16); git = system git 2.43.0; baseline = v0.5.0 release binary (grit-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz). GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM were isolated for all runs (the VM's global config enabled core.fsmonitor, commit signing and LFS filters, which would skew git); a minimal user.name/email config was used instead.
Harness: `grit-bench daily` was run once per scenario (`--only <id>`, headline rows also with `--baseline-grit`), because a baseline failure aborts an all-in-one run. v0.5.0 cannot run the blame, stash and log (--limit) headline commands, so those three rows have baseline=null with baseline_note (not substituted); the same run retried without --baseline-grit. Runs per tool are in each row (`runs`, 3 to 20 timed runs after 1 warmup, policy default). stddev_ms is null everywhere: the daily runner reports medians only. max_rss_kb is the peak RSS of the timed process tree. The runner's capped-run poll interval is already 1 ms on main, so no quantisation workaround was needed and no repo code was touched (the unmodified grit and grit-bench release binaries built from main were used). Fixtures were pre-generated with `grit-bench fixtures prepare` (git.git cloned at v2.47.0); the deep-history fixtures were built on demand by their scenarios.
Scenario set: all executable ids in grit-bench's daily registry (100). The two `test/*@smoke-fixture` registry ids are harness self-tests that are not available outside smoke mode and are omitted. New since 2026-10-20: commit/paths@synth-10k, commit/staged@synth-100k, status/paths@synth-100k, status/renamed@synth-10k, resolve/change-id@git-git, log/json-100@git-git, log/author-n50 and revs/* rows on the deep-history fixtures.
Noise re-runs: compared with daily/latest.json of 2026-10-20 (grit/git time ratio more than 20% worse, or peak-RSS ratio more than 30% worse). Re-ran each of these 3 more times (4 samples per tool; the reported median_ms and max_rss_kb are the median of the four per-sample medians/peaks; per-row `rerun` records the sample count and the first-pass grit/git ratio): diff/worktree@synth-10k, show/head@git-git, branch/delete@many-refs, bundle/create@synth-10k, commit/small@small, config/get@small, diff/staged@deep-tree, diff/worktree@big-blobs, diff/worktree@deep-tree, gc/default@synth-10k, repack/commit-graph@git-git, resolve/head-n@git-git, show/head@synth-10k, fsck/full@big-blobs. Outcome: config/get@small (2.44x -> 1.54x), resolve/head-n@git-git (2.79x -> 1.96x), commit/small@small (1.18x -> 1.15x) and diff/worktree@big-blobs (0.64x -> 0.68x) were mostly noise; show/head@git-git (6.5x), show/head@synth-10k (3.9x), diff/staged@deep-tree (4.2x), diff/worktree@deep-tree (4.7x), bundle/create@synth-10k (13x), gc/default@synth-10k (43.5x, yesterday 0.73x, grit also 4.6x git's peak RSS), repack/commit-graph@git-git (2.2x), branch/delete@many-refs (2.1x) and fsck/full@big-blobs (0.74x vs 0.52x yesterday) reproduced and look like real regressions or slowdowns versus yesterday's report.
Failures: worktree/add@synth-10k (grit worktree add creates a branch named after the target dir; harness reset leaves the branch so later runs fail), repack/full@git-git and fsck/full@git-git (grit reports a SHA-1 collision on real git.git v2.47.0 pack data: new regression, both passed or merely timed out on 2026-10-20), push/incremental-http@git-git (grit push over HTTP did not finish within the 1500 s cap; the same row timed out yesterday). For the three that abort on the first grit failure the git side was not recorded.
First attempt at the three *-http scenarios failed at setup because grit-http-server was not on PATH (only grit-cli and grit-utils had been built); I then built `grit-http-server` from the same main commit and re-ran them successfully (clone/http, fetch/incremental-http) with push/incremental-http hitting the cap.
Observations: the headline fetch, pull and push rows show grit far faster than git (and than v0.5.0). I spot-checked fetch by hand on the scenario's fixture: after the harness prepare step `grit fetch origin` took 25 ms and moved refs/remotes/origin/master to the remote tip (100 new commits), so those numbers reflect real work. The 2026-10-20 worktree/add row recorded grit at 0.0 ms, which is consistent with this same run-time failure being recorded as zero.
